purpose: Original standalone concepts for user selection; not inserted into onboarding UI
original_artwork: All compositions, paths and waveform geometry authored from scratch; no stock images or copied figures. Standard installed sans-serif glyph rendering; no fonts redistributed.
scientific_scope: Selected observed electrophysiological associations. Not a diagnostic map, quantitative power table, alertness scale, sound-to-brain transfer function, or predicted effect of auditory stimulation.
limits: Gamma is not a highest-alertness state.
Theta can occur in waking memory tasks.
Examples are non-exhaustive and regional/task dependent.
Five app band boundaries are a stated convention, not universal cutoffs.

claim_sources.claim: Band naming; characteristic beta and gamma contexts; drowsiness examples; deep NREM/alpha context
claim_sources.source: IFCN glossary, 2017, with app beta convention following its documented correction

claim_sources.claim: Posterior alpha during eyes-closed relaxed wakefulness
Theta and gamma during a particular healthy-human declarative-memory task (MEG)
claim_sources.source: Osipova et al., 2006, Theta and Gamma Oscillations Predict Encoding and Retrieval of Declarative Memory
claim_sources.scope: Original study ranges 4.5–8.5 and 60–90 Hz; diagrams use the app labels and disclose differing conventions.

claim_sources.claim: Sleep phases are not a monotonic low-to-high frequency or alertness ladder; REM can resemble waking activity
claim_sources.source: NIH NHLBI, Sleep Phases and Stages
